Description: Volunteers at the 3rd PatrasIQ research and technology exhibition (Patras, Greece, April 2016) each ranked six cities, drawn at random from a pool of 36, from highest to lowest cost of living. 392 rankings, 2352 rows. A ground truth is known (numbeo.com cost-of-living index, April 2016), highest first: san_francisco > zurich > new_york > lausanne > london > washington > boston > oslo > sydney > tokyo > dubai > copenhagen > doha > stockholm > melbourne > tel_aviv > munich > rome > brussels > toronto > maastricht > vienna > genoa > berlin > barcelona > montreal > lagos > nicosia > athens > istanbul > baghdad > patras > budapest > mexico_city > bucharest > mumbai; 74.1% of the pairs within rankings agree with it. Items are the place names in lowercase snake_case (new_york). One row per ranking x position; id = one ranking 1..n in PrefLib's order, resp = the position given (1 = highest). The same volunteers answered the population question (caragiannis_2017_patrasiq_population), but the source has no volunteer key, so the two tables cannot be joined by id. Some identical rankings repeat and are kept as recorded. Rankings layout (data/rankings/README.md).
Reference: Caragiannis, I., Chatzigeorgiou, X., Krimpas, G. A., & Voudouris, A. A. (2017). Optimizing Positional Scoring Rules for Rank Aggregation. Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 31(1). https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v31i1.10585. Distributed by PrefLib as dataset 00034 (Cities Survey), https://www.preflib.org/dataset/00034 (Mattei, N. & Walsh, T. 2013, PrefLib: A Library for Preferences, ADT 2013).
Notes: Script data/rankings/caragiannis_2017_patrasiq.py; design record data/rankings/design_tables.csv. Read from PrefLib 00034-00000001.soi (PrefLib-Data commit 220b7e5), a weighted profile expanded to one id per ranking. Ground truth recorded in the description and the design record's evidence. Licence: no licence is stated by PrefLib or the authors' pages. Original License = Permission via Email: Ioannis Caragiannis replied on 2026-11-20 'Sure, you can distribute our datasets.' to IRW's letter of 2026-11-15 (oneoff/email-drafts-2026-11-15/preflib/caragiannis_cities.txt), which offered CC BY 4.0 as the default licence; he did not name a licence, so the Derived License is CC BY 4.0. The letter proposed one table with the two questions as tasks; PrefLib's two files cannot be linked by volunteer, so each question is its own table.
